goal: Fix v7 migration crash on legacy coverage tables lacking source_file_set_fingerprint

summary.title: Fix v7 migration crash on legacy coverage tables lacking source_file_set_fingerprint
summary.what: Real v7 databases written by Sherlog 0.4.3 and earlier store a 13-column coverage table, while 0.4.4+ writers use 14 columns under the same shlog-v7-source-identity version string. The migrator now probes the column with PRAGMA table_info, hashes the shape the database actually has, and mixes a COV13/COV14 marker into the digest. It also cleans stale .v7.bak backup debris older than 24h, always keeping the newest.
summary.why: Upstream 0.4.4 added the coverage column without bumping INDEX_VERSION, so every explicit v7->v8 migration on a pre-0.4.4 database aborted with 'no such column: source_file_set_fingerprint' and left a fresh backup behind on each retry. Verified end to end against a real 0.4.4-era v7 database (143 sessions, 18260 messages): unfixed v0.6.0 aborts, the fixed build migrates fully.
summary.user_goal: Fix v7 migration crash on legacy coverage tables lacking source_file_set_fingerprint

decisions.point: How to read legacy coverage rows that may lack the column
decisions.chose: Probe with PRAGMA table_info and branch the SELECT instead of bumping the index version

decisions.point: Whether the two digest shapes must be distinguishable
decisions.chose: Yes: mix a COV13/COV14 marker so a missing column never equals an explicit NULL; the digest is only compared within one migration run, so no persisted contract changes

decisions.point: What to do about the .v7.bak debris the bug created
decisions.chose: Best-effort cleanup of backups older than 24h, keeping the newest one; never fatal

rejected.alternative: Bump INDEX_VERSION to a v7.1/v8 alias so the 13-column shape gets its own version string
rejected.reason: would force a full index rebuild on every 0.4.4+ user and reclassify existing healthy indexes for a purely additive upstream mistake

rejected.alternative: Treat the missing column as NULL inside the hash
rejected.reason: a missing column and an explicit NULL would then produce identical digests, hiding the schema-shape difference the fingerprint is meant to capture

review_notes: Upstream test fixtures modeled only the 0.4.4+ schema, which is how the crash escaped CI; new tests cover the 13-column path end to end
Validated against a real 0.4.4-era v7 database (143 sessions, 18260 messages): unfixed v0.6.0 aborts with the production error, the fixed build migrates fully and passes all verifiers
